images.prompt: Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama. A server rack about the height of a shoebox stands upright near the centre of a pale neutral tabletop. It is a brushed graphite frame with chamfered rails and fine machining marks, holding eight slim drive sleds in two columns, each faced with frosted acrylic. All sit dark except one near the top, where a small acid-lime status light blinks. To the left, a short frosted glass fan housing sits behind a graphite grille; to the right, an ivory card clipboard of blank log sheets lies squared beside a cold mug. A single graphite cable leaves the back of the rack in one tidy curve. A fine layer of dust rests on the top plate, undisturbed. Wide 16:9 landscape frame. The hero object sits slightly left of centre on the lower third, with the related objects extending to the right so the workflow reads left to right. Clean, generous negative space above. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: one large soft key light from the upper left at about 45 degrees, like diffused north-window daylight, with a gentle white bounce fill from the right; soft grounded contact shadows fall to the lower right. Camera: 100mm macro lens at f/4, eye level with the tabletop, three-quarter view. The hero object is tack sharp and the background melts into smooth, creamy blur on a seamless pale neutral sweep. Mood: calm, precise, orderly and quietly premium, like high-end editorial product photography. Strictly no people, figures, faces, hands or silhouettes. No readable text, letters, numbers, clock digits, logos, signage or user-interface graphics anywhere. No holograms, floating screens, robots with faces, dense cable tangles, carnival or circus elements, cartoon or plastic CGI look, oversaturated colour, lens flare or heavy vignette.

Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama, captured mid-disaster. The same rack is overheating. Every sled now glows milky white through its frosted front, and several have been shoved half out of their bays by the heat, with one tipping mid-fall toward the table. The acid-lime light that started it still blinks at the top, now lost in the glare. Heat shimmer rises above the frame, and the hot draught has lifted the log sheets off the clipboard: they curl and flip upward, one airborne above the mug. The fan housing's glass has fogged and its grille has bowed outward. The graphite cable has pulled taut and dragged the clipboard to the table edge. The top plate is dulled and faintly warped, and the dust on it has been blown into streaks pointing away from the rack. Wide 16:9 landscape frame, same layout and angle as the calm version of this scene. The hero object stays slightly left of centre, and the spread of the disaster runs to the right and toward the camera so its path can be traced back to the source. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: the same soft upper-left key and right-side bounce fill as a calm studio setup, unchanged, so the disorder reads as physical and real rather than theatrical. Airborne paper, grains and fragments catch the key light with crisp edge highlights. Camera: 85mm lens at f/5.6, same three-quarter tabletop angle, fast shutter freezing everything mid-air. Focus sits where the chain reaction started, and the spread softens into the depth of field. Mood: absurd but plausible, an orderly system that got out of hand, still clean and editorial. Photorealistic photograph of a vast handcrafted miniature landscape diorama. A long, dim underground hall stretches away between rows of squat graphite pillars toward a faint doorway of light at the far end. Its floor is drifted with grey-ivory paper dust, rippled like a cave floor. The rack lies toppled against one pillar at enormous scale, its frame bowed and its drive sleds jutting out like broken shelves, their frosted fronts crazed and cold. More sleds lie scattered across the floor in half-buried lines, and the old log sheets have fused into brittle drifts along the walls. Beside the rack, a slim graphite tracked carrier with a lime lift fork has just slid one fresh sled into a straightened bay, and a single lime status light on that sled now glows steady, the only light in the hall. Wide 16:9 panoramic frame. The main ruin anchors the left or centre foreground, terrain rolls back to a distant horizon on the upper third, and the lime recovery rig sits in the right midground. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: soft overcast late-afternoon daylight still falling from the upper left, with long soft shadows grounding the ruins and atmospheric haze fading distant forms into pale grey-green. Camera: wide 24mm view from a low vantage just above the terrain, deep focus through the midground, with a gentle tilt-shift falloff at the top and bottom edges so the vast scene still reads as a miniature diorama.
